mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and depressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% month-over-month triggers a demand pullback that depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST MoM change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not statistically significant at p < 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months indicates a persistent contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO MoM change < -1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both the federal funds rate and the 10-year Treasury yield (proxied by RSAFS) below their respective 5-year averages signals a broad-based easing in risk-free rates, which increases equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) above 0.5% for six consecutive months signals improving household purchasing power, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS MoM change > 0.5% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate coincident with a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month indicates a rapid labor market deterioration, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases AND PAYEMS MoM change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 10% for three consecutive months signals a robust residential investment cycle, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST MoM change > 10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered periods.
